name: Motor grader
subtitle: 16 ft (4.9 m) moldboard mine grader -- CAT 16 / GD825 / BG605 family
summary: The haul-road machine. A good road lets a loaded truck run faster, use less fuel and keep its tyres; a bad one costs more than the grader does. Graders keep the surface smooth and crowned, cut the drains, clear spillage and dress the berms.
safety: Trucks cannot see a grader close in front or behind them. Work with the beacon on and in radio contact with every truck on the road.
Grade with the traffic, not against it, and never park in a blind corner or over a crest.
Never stand in the articulation zone -- the frames swing together when the machine steers.
Leave windrows out of the travelled lane; a windrow can steer a truck tyre or hide a rock.
ar_tips: Walk to the front: the moldboard is angled so it sweeps material to one side -- you can see where the windrow would form.
Place it beside the 220 t dumper to see who must give way to whom on a haul road.

parts.label: Tyres (23.5R25)
parts.note: Six driven or steered tyres about 1.6 m tall. A grader rarely wears out tyres -- it saves them on the trucks. A 40.00R57 truck tyre costs many lakhs, and most are lost to cuts from rock spill the grader should have cleared.

parts.label: Rims & hubs
parts.note: Front wheels lean up to about 18 degrees so the grader can hold a line against the sideways push of an angled blade.

parts.label: Tandem drive
parts.note: Each side's two rear wheels are chain-driven from a tandem case that oscillates, so all four keep traction over rough ground. That is what lets a grader hold a blade height to a few centimetres.

parts.label: Front axle (steer & lean)
parts.note: Steering, wheel lean and oscillation all happen here. Combined with the articulation the grader can crab -- tandem offset from the front -- to keep its wheels off a freshly cut windrow.

parts.label: Front frame (gooseneck)
parts.note: The long beam from the cab to the front axle. Everything the blade does is hung from it, so its length is what makes a grader so good at smoothing: the blade averages out the bumps between the axles.

parts.label: Articulation joint
parts.note: The frame bends here, up to about 25 degrees each way. It halves the turning circle and lets the operator offset the rear wheels. Keep clear: the gap between frames closes with great force when the machine steers.

parts.label: Drawbar
parts.note: A-frame pulled from a ball joint at the front of the frame. It carries the circle and the blade, and is what the lift cylinders raise, lower and swing sideways.

parts.label: Circle (turntable)
parts.note: A geared ring that rotates the blade to any angle, and even right round for back-grading. Blade angle decides whether material rolls off the end or is carried.

parts.label: Moldboard (4.9 m)
parts.note: Angled about 30-45 degrees, the blade cuts high spots and rolls material along its face to fill the low ones, leaving a windrow. A mine road should keep a 2-3 % crossfall to shed water -- standing water is what makes potholes.

parts.label: Cutting edge & end bits
parts.note: Hardened, bolt-on and replaceable. A worn edge leaves a rounded, washboard surface no matter how good the operator is.

parts.label: Blade lift cylinders
parts.note: Raise, lower and tilt the blade independently at each end -- that is how a crossfall is cut. Never reach between the drawbar and the frame while the engine is running.

parts.label: Rear frame
parts.note: Carries the engine, transmission and tandems, and the cab just ahead of them.

parts.label: Engine compartment
parts.note: Diesel of about 220-250 kW and a powershift transmission. Graders work in a low gear at walking pace when cutting, and travel at up to about 45 km/h between jobs.

parts.label: Exhaust stack
parts.note: Exhaust and intake are kept high and to the rear, away from the operator's view forward.

parts.label: Cab with ROPS
parts.note: High, glassy cab ahead of the rear wheels so the operator can see both blade ends and the front tyres. Graders share the haul road with 220 t trucks whose drivers cannot see them: flashing beacon, buggy whip and radio contact, always.

parts.label: Cab glazing
parts.note: Glass down to the floor at the front, so the operator can see the blade toe and heel without leaning out.

parts.label: Rear ripper
parts.note: Breaks up a hard, compacted road surface or windrowed rock before the blade can cut it.

parts.label: 1.8 m person (for scale)
parts.note: A person in PPE, 1.8 m tall, standing clear of the machine. Use the scale toggle to hide them. In real AR at 1:1 you can simply walk up to the machine yourself.
